claims.text: Superconducting behavior in high-entropy alloys is primarily governed by electron–phonon coupling enhanced by configurational disorder.
High configurational disorder modifies local vibrational modes.
Disorder-induced modification of local vibrational modes causes phonon softening.
Phonon softening caused by disorder increases the electron–phonon coupling constant.
Electron–phonon coupling influences the superconducting transition temperature in conventional weak-coupling superconductors.
The proposed starting material is a disordered, single-phase alloy containing multiple principal elements.
Some superconducting high-entropy alloys exhibit weak-coupling, isotropic single-band s-wave BCS behavior.
Replacing a multicomponent HEA with a binary or ternary alloy reduces configurational entropy and chemical disorder.
Maintaining similar crystal structure and electron count provides a control intended to isolate configurational disorder.
Chemical disorder broadens local phonon modes.
The full HEA should have a higher electron–phonon coupling constant than the lower-disorder binary or ternary baseline.
The full HEA should have a lower Debye temperature than the lower-disorder baseline.
The full HEA should exhibit broader and softer phonon features than the lower-disorder baseline.
Changes in electron–phonon coupling should be accompanied by corresponding changes in Tc.
Differences in electron count or low-energy electronic structure can also affect Tc and confound attribution to disorder.
The McMillan relation can be used with Tc and Debye-temperature data to estimate the electron–phonon coupling constant.
The proposed disorder mechanism is expected to dominate only in weak-coupling BCS systems with structural phase and electron count controlled.
Failure of entropy reduction to change electron–phonon coupling, phonon broadening or softening, and Tc would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The core hypothesis attributes Tc variation primarily to configurational disorder, but the cited Ta–Nb–Zr–Hf–Ti HEA study reports comparable disorder at two compositions and explicitly excludes a disorder-driven origin for the observed Tc variation.
